# Search/Split String

![Search/Split String function icon](../../../assets/function-icons/functions/string/13-rechercher-premiere-occurrence.svg)

[String functions](index.md) · [All functions](../index.md)

Finds an occurrence and splits the string at that position.

## Types and connection rules

Scalar String, optional search String and I32 offset produce before-match String, match-and-remainder String and I32 match offset. Wire search or offset. Match Single Character is an editor option.

- Type resolution: `fixed`; result expression: `declared_output_type`.
- Implicit coercion: not enabled by this resolver; individual port policies remain explicit.
- Arrays: not accepted; lifting policy: `none`.

**Input count:** 3; this contract does not enable variadic inputs.

## Examples

These are real `.frog` documents from the same index used by Studio. Backend names and expected results describe the examples; they are not execution certificates.

- [Search/Split String — found](../../examples/string.search-split.found.md) — An exact byte substring search returns the prefix and matching suffix. A missing match returns offset -1 and an empty matching suffix. (`execution`, `studio-draft`).
- [Search/Split String — missing](../../examples/string.search-split.missing.md) — An exact byte substring search returns the prefix and matching suffix. A missing match returns offset -1 and an empty matching suffix. (`execution`, `studio-draft`).
- [Split String at a byte offset](../../examples/string.search-split.offset-only.md) — When search String is unwired, the offset alone splits the value. No search token or Enter-like validation is fabricated. (`execution`, `studio-draft`).
